/about.title: Who works here?

blocks.text: Keepers of Coffee, known around Rice as KOCs, are the baristas who keep Coffeehouse running. The key to why KOCs are so special? All employees are regular Rice students! We balance our academic schedules with our passion for making lots and lots of coffee, exactly how you want it. We take a lot of pride in making Coffeehouse a place where we, and all of Rice, can feel at home. It’s this dedication–and a healthy dose of shenanigans–that make Chaus, Chaus. Meet our managers for 2024-2025 here.

blocks.text: Rice Coffeehouse is a student run coffeehouse on Rice University's campus. We are managed and staffed by students with guidance from our two wonderful advisors Caitlin and Cristy. As a Student Run Business, Coffeehouse managers work together to make sure that the rent is paid, the products are served, the catering orders are filled, health code is followed, and a good time is had by all that come to Coffeehouse.

blocks.text: Since 2003, Katz has served some of Houston’s most highly-acclaimed and discriminating chefs and restaurant & coffeehouse owners. They specialize in small-batch, custom roasting while providing the finest coffee from our farmers around the globe. Their goal is to achieve perfection in every cup.  This commitment starts with sourcing the highest quality “green” beans and the close and careful attention we take in the roasting process. Katz is our exclusive provider of all coffee and coffee equipment. We are very lucky to have been working closely with them and serving their coffee since 2005. Coffeehouse wouldn’t be Coffeehouse without Katz!

blocks.text: At the tender age of 8 years old, our pastry chef Heather Davis began a tradition that would one day become a passion. Heather’s love of creating sweet treats was birthed from baking holiday cookies with her mother.  Although the native Houstonian initially took a traditional career path to become a teacher, she continued to develop her craft as a baker. Though Heather would often bring her fresh baked goods to her school just for the love of baking, her fellow teachers started placing orders, and encouraged her to sell them.  So in 2011 she made the life-changing decision to launch a bakery, Chic Sweets Fine Desserts.

blocks.text: Kraftsmen Baking was founded by Chef Scott Tycer in 2001. Chef Tycer, from highly acclaimed restaurants such as Aries and Gravitas, saw a void in Houston’s market for fresh, artisan bread; thus Kraftsmen Baking was born. All products are lovingly made by hand, using only the finest ingredients and no chemical preservatives. The flour used is top milled and free from bleaching agents and bromate. Kraftsmen provides sticky buns, chocolate croissants, and bear claws to Coffeehouse.

Their products are so sinfull that many of our customers ask, “Is this vegan?” Yes! It’s 100% vegan, including a selectionof gluten-free products. Sinfull is truly a Houston staple, and Coffeehouse is thrilled to serve their vegan cinnamon rolls and bars.

blocks.text: Coffeehouse is run by students for students and the Houston community. Though we may be currently closed, we are committed to combating the systems of oppression upon which this country was founded. We will work to uplift Black and other marginalized voices. As the General Manager of Coffeehouse, I want to make it clear that Coffeehouse stands in solidarity with the Black community against racial injustices.

blocks.text: In recent years, Coffeehouse has defined its mission statement as focusing on environmental sustainability. However, we are first a community driven by people. There will be no sustainable future if communities continue to experience systematic oppression. Inequality and oppression constantly affect the lives of marginalized people, so it is imperative that our support lasts beyond this news cycle.

blocks.text: As a long term financial commitment by Coffeehouse, I am announcing the Bean Fund, an annual $1000 dedicated towards causes of social justice as it relates to environmental sustainability. The fund is meant to provide flexibility and ensure our approach towards environmental sustainability is intersectional. We will first be donating 750 dollars split across three organizations: Black Lives Matter Houston, Texas Organizing Project, and BLMHTX; a fourth donation will be decided by our team at a later date, totaling $1000.
